source: TRAI and DoT numbering-plan announcements, plus community-reported ranges
notes: Categories describe how a series is allocated, not whether a call is fraudulent. Every COMMUNITY entry is a user observation and ships disabled. Rules are scoped to both SIMs because a numbering series is a property of the caller, not of the line; which SIMs actually enforce them is the per-SIM protection switch, not the scope. An upgrade never rewrites a scope the user has changed.

rules.name: 1600 Transactional Service
rules.description: Service and transactional calls from banks, insurers and government. Not marketing.

rules.name: 1601 Transactional Service
rules.description: Service and transactional calls from other sectors such as utilities and logistics.

rules.name: 160 Service Series
rules.description: The wider 160 service range, for any allocation not covered by 1600 or 1601.

rules.name: 1800 Toll Free
rules.description: Indian toll-free numbers. Usually a company's own customer service line.

rules.name: 1860 Customer Service
rules.description: Chargeable customer-service range used by many banks and insurers.

rules.name: 140 Promotional Calls
rules.description: India's regulated series for promotional and telemarketing calls. Blocking it stops marketing, not service messages.

rules.name: 0900 Premium Rate
rules.description: Premium-rate service series. Calls in this range can be chargeable.

rules.name: Unknown callers
rules.description: Calls where the network supplied no usable caller ID.

rules.name: Private callers
rules.description: Callers who have deliberately withheld their number.

rules.name: International callers
rules.description: Any caller with a country code other than +91. International is not the same as unwanted.
